punchline: Google search costs nothing because someone else is the paying customer.
thirty_sec: Osterwalder and Pigneur treat Free as a pattern: one customer group gets the value at no cost, and another part of the model pays for it. They sort it into three kinds. Advertising is Google's: advertisers pay so users can search without limit. Premium services keep a basic version free and charge for an upgrade. Continuing purchases give away or cheapen the first item, like a coffee machine that needs capsules.
